# 12-Week Strength and Hypertrophy Programme

**Client:** 26F, recreational lifter
**Start date:** Monday 1 June 2026
**End date:** Sunday 23 August 2026
**Goals:** Strength gains on the main lifts and body composition improvement (lean mass up, body fat down)

## Programme Overview

- **Format:** 4 sessions per week, Upper/Lower split (Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B)
- **Training days:** Mon (Upper A), Tue (Lower A), Thu (Upper B), Fri (Lower B). Wed, Sat and Sun are rest or light activity.
- **Session length:** 60–75 minutes
- **Intensity:** Measured by RIR (reps in reserve). RIR 2 means you could have done 2 more clean reps.
- **Progression:** Add load when all prescribed sets hit the top of the rep range with good form at the target RIR. Otherwise hold the load and aim for more reps the following week.
- **Warm-up:** 5–8 minutes of low-intensity cardio, then 2–3 ramp-up sets on the first exercise of each session.

Hormonal contraception does not require changes to the programme. Training continues the same across the whole pill cycle, including the placebo week. Ask her to tell you about any new symptoms, medications or changes to her health so you can adjust the plan.

## Session Templates

**Upper A (Mon)**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps (Phase 1 / 2 / 3) |
|---|---|
| Barbell bench press | 3×8–12 / 4×5–6 / 4×4–6 |
| Chest-supported row | 3×8–12 / 3×8–10 / 3×8–10 |
| Seated dumbbell overhead press | 3×8–12 / 3×6–8 / 3×6–8 |
| Lat pulldown | 3×10–12 / 3×8–10 / 3×8–10 |
| Triceps pushdown | 2×12–15 / 2×10–12 / 2×10–12 |
| Dumbbell curl | 2×12–15 / 2×10–12 / 2×10–12 |

**Lower A (Tue)**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps (Phase 1 / 2 / 3) |
|---|---|
| Back squat | 3×8–12 / 4×5–6 / 4×4–6 |
| Romanian deadlift | 3×8–12 / 3×6–8 / 3×6–8 |
| Leg press | 3×12–15 / 3×10–12 / 3×10–12 |
| Lying leg curl | 3×10–12 / 3×10–12 / 3×10–12 |
| Standing calf raise | 3×12–15 / 3×10–12 / 3×10–12 |
| Plank | 3×30–45 s / 3×40–60 s / 3×40–60 s |

**Upper B (Thu)**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps (Phase 1 / 2 / 3) |
|---|---|
| Incline dumbbell press | 3×8–12 / 4×6–8 / 4×5–8 |
| Seated cable row | 3×10–12 / 3×8–10 / 3×8–10 |
| Dumbbell lateral raise | 3×12–15 / 3×12–15 / 3×12–15 |
| Face pull | 3×12–15 / 3×12–15 / 3×12–15 |
| Close-grip bench or dips (assisted if needed) | 2×8–12 / 3×6–10 / 3×6–10 |
| Hammer curl | 2×10–12 / 2×10–12 / 2×10–12 |

**Lower B (Fri)**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps (Phase 1 / 2 / 3) |
|---|---|
| Trap bar deadlift | 3×6–10 / 4×4–6 / 4×3–5 |
| Bulgarian split squat (each leg) | 3×8–12 / 3×8–10 / 3×8–10 |
| Hip thrust | 3×10–12 / 3×8–12 / 3×8–12 |
| Leg extension | 3×12–15 / 2×12–15 / 2×12–15 |
| Seated calf raise | 2×12–15 / 2×12–15 / 2×12–15 |
| Pallof press (each side) | 3×10 / 3×10 / 3×10 |

## Phase 1: Foundation and Hypertrophy Base (Weeks 1–4)

The aim is to learn the movements, build work capacity, and accumulate training volume.

- **Week 1 (1–7 June):** Use the Phase 1 set and rep ranges at RIR 3. Focus on technique and find working loads. Record every load. Complete baseline testing (see below) on Monday, before the first session.
- **Week 2 (8–14 June):** Same exercises at RIR 2–3. Add load where you hit the top of the rep range with good form.
- **Week 3 (15–21 June):** Same exercises at RIR 2. Push the working sets harder.
- **Week 4 (22–28 June):** Deload. Use the same exercises with half the working sets (for example, 2 sets instead of 3 on main lifts) at RIR 4–5, with loads about 10% lower than your Week 3 numbers. This lets you recover before Phase 2.

## Phase 2: Strength-Hypertrophy (Weeks 5–8)

Main lifts shift to heavier loads, and accessories stay in the hypertrophy range.

- **Week 5 (29 June–5 July):** Use Phase 2 set and rep ranges at RIR 2–3. Work up to a load you can do for 5–6 reps on the main lifts at RIR 2. Reset your loads from Week 4's numbers.
- **Week 6 (6–12 July):** RIR 2. Add load to main lifts when you complete all sets at the top of the range.
- **Week 7 (13–19 July):** RIR 1–2. Heaviest accumulation week. Keep form strict.
- **Week 8 (20–26 July):** Deload. Halve the working sets on main lifts, RIR 4, loads about 10% lower than Week 7. Retest 1–2 main lifts at the end of the week only if she feels fully recovered.

## Phase 3: Strength Peak (Weeks 9–12)

Main lifts drop to lower reps and heavier loads. Accessories are maintained.

- **Week 9 (27 July–2 August):** Phase 3 ranges at RIR 2. Establish new working loads for 3–5 reps.
- **Week 10 (3–9 August):** RIR 1–2. Add load where possible.
- **Week 11 (10–16 August):** RIR 1. Top week for main lift work. Accessories stay at Phase 3 volume. Avoid training to failure on squats and deadlifts.
- **Week 12 (17–23 August):** Lighter week. Halve main lift sets, RIR 3–4. Retest body composition and strength on Monday (17 August) before the Upper A session. Repeat the baseline protocol from Week 1.

## Baseline and Final Testing

Test in Week 1 and Week 12, under the same conditions (same time of day, same rest and nutrition approach where possible).

- **Body weight:** Fasted, morning, after toilet, before breakfast. Average over three mornings.
- **Waist circumference:** At the navel, relaxed breath.
- **Hip and thigh circumference:** Measure at the widest points.
- **Body composition:** Use the same method at both points (skinfolds, BIA, or DEXA if available). Consistency matters more than the device.
- **Progress photos:** Front, side and back, same lighting and posture.
- **Strength:** Estimate 1RM from a 3–5 rep max on back squat, trap bar deadlift, bench press and overhead press, or use a submaximal estimate if she is uncomfortable with heavy singles. Use a warm-up protocol and stop at RIR 1 for safety.

## Nutrition

- **Protein:** 1.6–2.2 g per kg of body weight per day, split across 3–5 meals (about 0.4 g/kg per meal). Good sources include lean meats, fish, eggs, Greek yoghurt, tofu and whey.
- **Calories:**
  - If body fat reduction is the priority, aim for a modest deficit of about 10–15% below maintenance. Track weekly averages and adjust if weight drops faster than about 0.5–0.7% of body weight per week.
  - If she is lean or the priority is building muscle, eat at maintenance or a small surplus (about 100–200 kcal/day).
  - Body recomposition is realistic for a recreational lifter, especially in the first 12 weeks.
- **Carbohydrates:** Include carbs in the 2–3 meals around training to fuel performance. Adjust the total to the calorie target.
- **Fats:** Keep about 20–30% of calories from fat, with an emphasis on unsaturated sources.
- **Fibre and micronutrients:** Aim for vegetables and fruit at most meals. Consider a basic multivitamin if her diet is restricted.
- **Hydration:** Roughly 30–35 ml per kg of body weight per day, more on training days and in hot weather.
- **Creatine monohydrate:** 3–5 g per day is an evidence-based option for strength and lean mass. Only start it if she has no kidney issues and has checked with her doctor.

## Recovery

- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours per night. Sleep is one of the biggest drivers of recovery and body composition. Track it weekly.
- **Rest days:** Keep Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday for rest or easy movement such as walking, cycling or mobility. Aim for 7,000–10,000 steps per day.
- **Deload weeks:** Weeks 4, 8 and 12 are built in. Do not skip them, even if she feels good.
- **Monitoring:** Ask her to rate sleep, soreness, energy and motivation from 1 to 5 each week. Watch for a drop in performance across consecutive sessions, which can signal under-recovery.
- **Stress and life load:** Adjust volume if work, study or life stress spikes. Dropping one accessory set is better than missing a session.

## Weekly Check-In

Each week, review:
1. Attendance and completion of all sessions
2. Logged loads and reps against targets
3. Body weight trend (7-day average)
4. Sleep, energy and soreness scores
5. Any pain or joint discomfort (stop and reassess if pain is sharp or worsening)
6. Adherence to protein and calorie targets

Make changes only when two or more of these indicate a problem. Keep the core programme consistent to make the results easy to read.
